source_evidence: Knowing your time horizon and your personal tolerance for risk is helpful.
answer: Risk tolerance is how comfortable you are with the possibility that investments may fluctuate or lose value. Consider it alongside your time horizon—the length of time before you expect to use the money. For example, someone investing for retirement decades away has time to manage market fluctuations, while someone who prefers a more conservative approach should take that preference into account. These factors can help guide the types of investment products you choose.
